questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. It is unquestionably evident that this virus brought misery and grief into the lives of people of other professions too.

B. Covid-19 changed the form and face of every field in the world. It did not leave any field untouched.

C. One of the most affected areas is education. Millions of students all over the world could not get a proper education.

D. Millions of teachers who are working, specifically in private educational institutes, were not paid a full salary during the pandemic.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "BCDA"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• Let's look at the correct sequence of the passage. 
 
• Statement B is the opening sentence of the passage which explains that every field in the world has transformed because to COVID-19. No field was left unaffected by it.
 
• Statement C is the second sentence of the passage which explains that education is one of the most severely impacted fields. Millions of youngsters worldwide were unable to receive a quality education.
 
• Statement D is the third sentence of the passage which explains that during the epidemic, millions of teachers who are currently employed—particularly those in private educational institutions were not paid their full salaries.
 
• Statement A is the last sentence of the passage which shows that It is without a doubt clear that this illness caused suffering and anguish in the lives of persons who worked in other professions as well.

Hence, the correct sequence is B, C, D, A

The correct answer is option 2.

The correct passage is: ***B**. Covid-19 changed the form and face of every field in the world. It did not leave any field untouched. **C**. One of the most affected areas is education. Millions of students all over the world could not get a proper education. **D**. Millions of teachers who are working, specifically in private educational institutes, were not paid a full salary during the pandemic. **A**. It is unquestionably evident that this virus brought misery and grief into the lives of people of other professions too.*

**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, select the one that gives its correct order.**

A. He told his friends that his difficulties were a sign of God’s confidence in him.

B. A businessman remained cheerful even though he suffered one catastrophe after another.

C. Therefore, when he was serving in the armed forces too, his senior officer had chosen him for dangerous missions because he knew he could be trusted.

D. First, his son had a serious accident and then he had huge losses in his business, but he was not perturbed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **BDAC.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• On reading the sentences, we can comprehend that the passage is all about Businessman and his life story.
 
• The first sentence will be sentence B as it tells us about the businessman.
 
• The second sentence will be sentence D as it tells us about the life of a businessman what has happened in his life.
 
• The third sentence will be sentence A as it tells us that the businessman about his life to his friends and they told him to have faith in God.
 
• The fourth sentence will be sentence C as it is the only sentence Left.

**So the correct passage is**- *A businessman remained cheerful even though he suffered one catastrophe after another. First, his son had a serious accident and then he had huge losses in his business, but he was not perturbed. He told his friends that his difficulties were a sign of God’s confidence in him. Therefore, when he was serving in the armed forces too, his senior officer had chosen him for dangerous missions because he knew he could be trusted.*

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. It is almost a definition of a gentleman to say he is one who never inflicts pain

B. He is mainly occupied in merely removing the obstacles which hinder the free and unembarrassed action of those about him, and he concurs with their movements rather than takes the initiative himself.

C. The true gentleman in like manner carefully avoids whatever may cause a jar or a jolt in the minds of those with whom he is cast; all clashing of opinion, or collision of feeling, all restraint, or suspicion, or gloom, or resentment; his great concern being to make everyone at their ease and at home.

D. His benefits may be considered as parallel to what are called comforts or conveniences in arrangements of a personal nature: like an easy chair or a good fire, which do their part in dispelling cold and fatigue, though nature provides both means of rest and animal heat without them
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **ABCD**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The paragraph discusses the characteristics of a true gentleman, who avoids causing discomfort or conflict to those around him.
 
• Sentence **A **provides a definition of a gentleman as someone who does not inflict pain.
 
• Sentence **B **introduces the idea that the gentleman's main role is to remove obstacles and follow the lead of others.
 
• Sentence **C **elaborates on the gentleman's avoidance of conflict and his focus on making everyone feel at ease.
 
• Sentence **D **compares the gentleman's actions to the comforts and conveniences that make life easier, but are not essential.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• '**BADC**' starts with the wrong sentence and rearranges the other sentences in a different order.
 
• '**DCBA**' puts the definition of a gentleman last, rather than first.
 
• '**DBAC**' starts with the idea of the gentleman avoiding conflict, but then jumps to the comparison with comforts and conveniences before elaborating further.

questions.question:
**Some sentences are given below. While the first and the last sentences (1 and 2) are in the correct order, the sentences in between are jumbled up. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

1.“Do you still recognise me?” I asked.

A. The woman looked at me searchingly.

B. “I am Mrs. S’s daughter”.

C. I came closer and stood on the step.

D. She opened the door a little.

2. She kept staring at me in silence.
questions.solution:
The correct order is: **BADC**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first sentence (**1**) sets the context for the paragraph and introduces the speaker.

 
 
• The second sentence (**B**) provides important information about the speaker's identity.
 
• The third sentence (**A**) describes the woman's reaction to the speaker's question.
 
• The fourth sentence (**D**) gives details about the physical setting and action.
 
• The fifth sentence (**C**) states the approaching and positioning.
 
 
 
• The last sentence (**2**) concludes the paragraph by describing the woman's reaction.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

**Arranged sentences**: ***1**.“Do you still recognise me?” I asked. **B**. “I am Mrs. S’s daughter”. **A**. The woman looked at me searchingly. **D**. She opened the door a little. **C**. I came closer and stood on the step. **2**. She kept staring at me in silence.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• (**BDAC**): This order doesn't make sense as it jumps from the woman's reaction (B) to the speaker's approach (D) before providing information about the speaker's identity (A).
 
• (**BACD**): This order is close to the correct answer but puts the speaker's approach (C) too early in the paragraph.
 
• (**BCAD**): This order also doesn't make sense as it jumps from the woman's reaction (B) to the speaker's approach (C) without providing information about the speaker's identity (A).

questions.question:
**Direction: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.**

(A) that further treatment

(B) useless

(C) the doctor concluded

(D) would be
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "CADB."** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence follows the subject-verb-Object (SVO) structure.
 
• **"The doctor"** is the subject, and** "concluded" **is the verb. So the first part must be C.
 
• **"That further treatment"** is the first part of the object. So, it must be A.
 
• The phrase **"that further treatment"** serves as a subordinating conjunction, connecting the doctor's conclusion to the statement about uselessness.
 
• The word **"useless"** is an adjective modifying the noun** "treatment." **So the last part must be the pair** DB.**
 
• The correct answer is option 1.

 

**Correct sentence**: *The doctor concluded that further treatment would be useless.*

questions.question:
**Directions: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.**

A. I sow a seed.

B. I saw the sapling.

C. I saw the sprout.

D. I saw the plant.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'ACBD'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's first understand the meaning of the given words which are given in the sentences-
 
 
• **Seed**→ A seed is the small, hard part of a plant from which a new plant grows.
 
• **Sapling**→ A sapling is a young tree.
 
• **Sprout**→ When plants, vegetables, or seeds sprout, they produce new shoots or leaves.
 
• **Plant**→ A plant is a living thing that grows in the earth and has a stem, leaves, and roots.
 
 
 
• **Hence according to the meaning of the words→ **
 
 
• *We put seed, then sprout will grow or develop, then sapling will come out a small plant and then the plant.*
 
 

**So the correct sentence is-*** I sow a seed I saw the sprout I saw the sapling I saw the plant.*

Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

Q. in the present international scenario, it is necessary and

R. and winning over the support of their counterparts in other countries

S. services of Members of Parliament effectively for sensitizing
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

questions.question:
**Direction: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.**

P. that a glance from the window seemed simply to prove

Q. with such dignity of motion

R. the great Pullman was whirling onward

S. that the plains of Texas were pouring eastward
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"RQPS."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• While arranging the parts of the sentence given in options, we have to find some grammatical or contextual connections between them__, so let’s find out.
 
• In this sentence, we can see that there are different parts like Subject, indirect object, subject of subordinating clause and verb, indirect object, and direct object.
 
• The sentence talks about the view from a moving train in Texas.
 
• The first part of the sentence is** "the great Pullman was whirling onward" **which sets the scene.
 
• The second part is** "with such dignity of motion" **which describes the movement of the train.
 
• The third part is **"that the plains of Texas were pouring eastward" **which describes the view from the train window.
 
• The fourth part is** "that a glance from the window seemed simply to prove"** which suggests that the view was so spectacular that a mere glance was enough to appreciate it.
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

 

**Correct sentence**: *The great Pullman was whirling onward with such dignity of motion that a glance from the window seemed simply to prove that the plains of Texas were pouring eastward.*

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

P. American political economist Mancur Olson, who wrote in 1965

Q. the problems of collective action were popularized by the

R. that coercion or some other device must be present in order

S. for a group of individuals to act in their common interest
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **QPRS**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this arrangement, the sentence starts with the introduction of the problems of collective action being popularized. This provides the context for the subsequent parts.
 
 
• **Q. **"The problems of collective action were popularized by the"
 
• **P. **"American political economist Mancur Olson, who wrote in 1965"
 
 
 
• These two parts go together as they establish who popularized the problems of collective action and when it happened. Mancur Olson, an American political economist, is mentioned as the individual responsible for bringing attention to these problems through his writing in 1965.
 
 
• **R.** "that coercion or some other device must be present in order"
 
• **S.** "for a group of individuals to act in their common interest"
 
 
 
• The last two parts connect to form a logical explanation. It states that in order for a group of individuals to act in their common interest, coercion or some other mechanism is necessary. This concludes the sentence by providing a solution or conclusion related to the problems of collective action.
 
• By following the order **QPRS**, the sentence maintains a logical flow by introducing the problem, establishing the authority, and providing an explanation or solution.

 

**Correct Arrangement**__: *The problems of collective action were popularized by the American political economist Mancur Olson, who wrote in 1965 that coercion or some other device must be present in order for a group of individuals to act in their common interest.*

questions.question:
Some parts of a few sentences have been jumbled up, and labelled A, B, C and D. Select the option that gives the correct sequence in which these parts can be rearranged to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence.

My years in my father’s house

A. would have been unbearable had

B. the feel of his hand clutching mine, his

C. I not had my brother. I never forgot

D. refusal to abandon me. Perhaps he and I would have been close even otherwise.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **correct sequence** of these sentences is **ACBD**. Here's why:
 
• "My years in my father’s house" is the main clause, which can stand by itself as a complete sentence.
 
• **"A. **would have been unbearable had" is the start of the next part of the sentence.
 
 
• **It provides a continuation** to the main clause, implying that something made the years bearable.
 
 
 
• **"C. **I not had my brother." This sentence fits well with the previous part (A) as it provides the answer to what made the years bearable - having a brother.
 
 
• **It forms a complete and meaningful sentence** when put after A, "My years in my father’s house would have been unbearable had I not had my brother."
 
• "I never forgot" is the continuation of the first part of the sentence, focusing on the protagonist's memories related to his brother.
 
 
 
• **"B. **the feel of his hand clutching mine, his" This sentence logically follows the previous part (C) as it provides more specific memories of his brother.
 
• **"D. **refusal to abandon me. Perhaps he and I would have been close even otherwise."
 
 
• This **sentence fits well **at the end as it rounds off the sentiment of the previous parts and completes the overall thought.
 
 

Therefore, the** complete sentence** is: *"My years in my father’s house would have been unbearable had I not had my brother. I never forgot the feel of his hand clutching mine, his refusal to abandon me. Perhaps he and I would have been close even otherwise." Hence, the correct sequence is ACBD.*
